name: South Dakota Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Chislic, Bison & Walleye
description:
South Dakota's restaurants, from chislic in Sioux Falls to bison and walleye in Rapid City.

South Dakota Eats is a free guide to eating in South Dakota: 13 places for chislic and 14 for bison and walleye that we checked by hand, plus 2,132 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 234 towns, from Sioux Falls and Brookings to Rapid City, Aberdeen and the Black Hills. No account, no ads.

SOUTH DAKOTA GUIDES
• Chislic: cubed lamb or beef, fried or grilled, from The Alibi's Monday-night lamb in Sioux Falls to Rapid City's Dakotah Steakhouse and The Pheasant in Brookings.
• Bison & Walleye: Rapid City's bison and walleye, from Tally's Silver Spoon to Shipwrecks.
• James Beard Honors: The Pheasant, a 2024 America's Classic, and 2025-26 semifinalists in Sioux Falls and Custer.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "chislic", "bison", "walleye".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a visitor bureau's own guide or listing or the James Beard Foundation's announcement. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept only when the listing is high-confidence. In Sioux Falls, places show the City's own two most recent inspection scores, as the City publishes them and dated; elsewhere the Department of Health's reports are search-only, so each place links to its search. The app computes no grades. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings. Newer restaurant data downloads from the South Dakota Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of South Dakota, its Department of Health or the City of Sioux Falls), any tribal nation, the South Dakota Department of Tourism or any visitor bureau, any university or team, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and the City of Sioux Falls (CC BY 4.0), among others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: South Dakota Eats is a free guide to restaurants in South Dakota (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: chislic, and bison and walleye, 21 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a visitor bureau's own guide or listing or the James Beard Foundation, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 2,132 restaurants, cafés and bars in 234 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Chislic (or Bison & Walleye, James Beard Honors, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it. Sioux Falls places show the City of Sioux Falls' two most recent published inspection scores with a link to the City's list; places elsewhere link to the South Dakota Department of Health's inspection search. The app shows no grades.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("chislic", "bison", "walleye").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside South Dakota (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on South Dakota, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "SD Eats" is the Home Screen name of "South Dakota Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the South Dakota Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the City of Sioux Falls' open restaurant-inspection and alcohol-license data (CC BY 4.0, attributed in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of visitor-bureau pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/south-dakota-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers South Dakota; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution in the app.
